body.statement: The actual compact-polyhedral overlap with Theorem 4 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local} is a proper subclass of the proposed two-dimensional regime: \[\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2.\] The inclusion follows from \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subseteq\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\subseteq\mathcal G_2\), while strictness is certified by the triangular game in \(\mathrm{prop:coexistence-witness}\), which belongs to \(\mathcal G_2\) but not to \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\), and hence not to \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\). Thus \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\) applies both to every game in the compact-polyhedral overlap and to at least one asymmetric game outside that overlap. Separately, for every \(\mathsf G\in\mathcal G_p^{\mathrm{cs}}\) whose modulus extremizer generates an antipodal least-favorable pair, that two-point prior and its Bayes rule satisfy the saddle conditions in \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\), so the resulting rule and value agree with the compact-polyhedral specialization of Yata2025Optimal. No inclusion between \(\mathcal G_p\) and the full published Assumption-5 class is asserted.
body.justification: The proposition proves the only strict-extension statement used in the proposal: the new two-dimensional class strictly contains the actual compact-polyhedral Theorem 4 overlap, with strictness supplied by an explicit asymmetric game.
body.gap: Assumption 5 with Theorem 4 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local covers a directionally differentiable centrosymmetric class, and Yata2025Optimal gives the antipodal centered benchmark. This proposition compares only on the defined compact-polyhedral overlap and does not claim that the proposed class contains the full published Assumption-5 class.
body.consumer: Researchers can identify exactly when the published centered solver is recovered and when the asymmetric all-saddle analysis supplies genuinely additional admissible games.
